title: Round 4 — Deep Cuts: Provence, Dinos & British Rock

questions.question: At which London stadium did Queen play their famous 20-minute Live Aid set on 13 July 1985?
questions.note: Queen's Live Aid set was later voted the greatest live rock performance of all time.

questions.question: Fontaine-de-Vaucluse, the immense spring feeding the River Sorgue, gives its name to a whole type of powerful rising karst spring. What adjective describes such springs worldwide?
questions.note: Hydrogeologists call rising karst springs 'Vauclusian' after Fontaine-de-Vaucluse, the largest karst spring in metropolitan France.

questions.question: In both Crichton's novel and the 1993 Jurassic Park film, the automated park tour is voiced by a real, named stage-and-screen actor whom Hammond 'spared no expense' to hire. Who was he?
questions.note: The novel names the genuine Richard Kiley as the tour narrator — the one expense Hammond really did splash on.

questions.question: The 'Four des Navettes' (1781), Marseille's oldest bakery, stands on the old sacred way leading to which Marseille abbey?
questions.note: The boat-shaped orange-blossom navettes, blessed at Candlemas, evoke the boat of the holy Marys and are tied to the Abbaye Saint-Victor.

questions.question: On what date in 1944 did the Allies launch Operation Dragoon, the amphibious landing on the coast of Provence known as the 'second D-Day'?
questions.note: Dragoon landed American, French and Allied forces between Le Lavandou and Saint-Raphaël to open a second front in southern France.

questions.question: English speakers say 'walkie-talkie'; in French the same handheld two-way radio is known by what name, with the two halves swapped round?
questions.note: French simply reverses the order of the English original.

questions.question: Thanks largely to the Camargue within its territory, Arles is mainland France's largest commune by area. Roughly how large is it?
questions.note: Arles covers roughly 759 km² — by far the largest commune in metropolitan France, despite only about 50,000 residents.

questions.question: Which British-born actress and singer recorded the 1969 duet 'Je t'aime... moi non plus' with Serge Gainsbourg?
questions.note: London-born Jane Birkin's duet topped the UK chart — the first foreign-language song to do so — despite being banned in several countries.

questions.question: The AOP black olives of Nyons — France's first olive appellation (1994) — are made exclusively from which single olive variety?
questions.note: Nyons olives and oil use only the wrinkled, cocoa-and-truffle-scented Tanche, grown in the Baronnies of northern Provence.

questions.question: In The Lost World: Jurassic Park (1997), which British actor played the big-game hunter Roland Tembo, who comes to Isla Sorna hoping to bag a male Tyrannosaurus?
questions.note: Spielberg cast the Lancashire-born Postlethwaite to embody the 'Great White Hunter' archetype in the sequel.

questions.question: In which year did the Provençal poet Frédéric Mistral win the Nobel Prize in Literature for reviving the Provençal language?
questions.note: Mistral shared the 1904 Nobel and founded the Félibrige society to preserve Provençal language and culture.

questions.question: On a French restaurant menu, which course is 'une entrée'?
questions.note: In France 'entrée' means the first course, unlike in the United States where it means the main course.

questions.question: At which London studios did Pink Floyd record their 1973 album 'The Dark Side of the Moon'?
questions.note: The album was recorded in 1972–73 at EMI Studios, now world-famous as Abbey Road Studios.

questions.question: Cézanne painted the Montagne Sainte-Victoire endlessly, but its true summit is not the conspicuous Croix de Provence. What is the ridge's actual highest peak called?
questions.note: The Pic des Mouches, at 1,011 m, is the real high point, well east of the more visible Croix de Provence.

questions.question: The Indominus rex in Jurassic World can camouflage its skin. Which animal's DNA, spliced in by Dr Henry Wu, gave it the colour-changing chromatophore cells?
questions.note: Cuttlefish genes, added to help it withstand rapid growth, also let the hybrid change skin colour and blend in.

questions.question: A red Bandol AOC wine must contain at least what minimum proportion of the Mourvèdre grape?
questions.note: Bandol is Mourvèdre's great French stronghold, requiring at least 50% in reds and rosés, with top estates going far higher.

questions.question: In 1793 a young Napoleon Bonaparte first made his name by driving a British-led fleet out of which fortified French Mediterranean naval port?
questions.note: French royalists had handed Toulon to a British fleet under Admiral Samuel Hood; Bonaparte's artillery forced its withdrawal in December 1793.

questions.question: In a French hair salon, if you ask for 'un brushing', what are you getting?
questions.note: 'Brushing' is a French anglicism for drying and styling the hair with a round brush and a hairdryer.

questions.question: The Étang de Berre, the great brackish lagoon west of Marseille, meets the Mediterranean through a single narrow shipping channel at Martigues. What is that channel called?
questions.note: The 6.5 km Canal de Caronte at Martigues is the lagoon's only natural outlet to the sea.

questions.question: Among the Provençal 'treize desserts', the 'quatre mendiants' (four beggars) are which four dried fruits and nuts?
questions.answer: Figs, almonds, walnuts (or hazelnuts) and raisins
questions.note: Their colours recall the habits of the four mendicant orders — Franciscans, Dominicans, Carmelites and Augustinians.

questions.question: Who was the guitarist in David Bowie's backing band the Spiders from Mars on the 1972 album 'Ziggy Stardust'?
questions.note: Mick Ronson played guitar, with Trevor Bolder on bass and Mick Woodmansey on drums, as Bowie's Spiders from Mars.

questions.question: On which island off Cannes was the mysterious 'Man in the Iron Mask' held prisoner during the reign of Louis XIV?
questions.note: The masked prisoner was held in the Fort Royal on Île Sainte-Marguerite, largest of the Lérins islands, before being moved to the Bastille.

questions.question: In France, a pharmacy is signalled to the street by an illuminated sign in the shape of a cross of what colour?
questions.note: French pharmacies use a green cross, adopted after a 1913 law barred them from the red cross of the Red Cross.

questions.question: The original Jurassic Park won three Academy Awards, all technical: Best Visual Effects, Best Sound, and which third?
questions.note: Its three 1994 Oscars were Visual Effects, Sound, and Sound Effects Editing, with Gary Rydstrom winning two of them.

questions.question: Cap Canaille, rising above the sea between Cassis and La Ciotat, is among the highest sea cliffs in France. Roughly how high is it?
questions.note: Cap Canaille climbs about 394 m straight from the Mediterranean, ranking among the tallest maritime cliffs in the country.

questions.question: In the August 1995 'Battle of Britpop', which Blur single beat Oasis's 'Roll With It' to the UK number-one spot?
questions.note: Both singles came out on 14 August 1995; Blur's 'Country House' outsold Oasis to take number one.

questions.question: The dish name 'brandade' comes from the Occitan verb 'brandar'. What does that verb mean?
questions.note: The salt-cod-and-olive-oil emulsion of Nîmes is named for the vigorous stirring that binds it.

questions.question: In Jurassic Park, which rival BioSyn scientist pays Dennis Nedry to steal the dinosaur embryos, handing him the disguised Barbasol can in San José?
questions.note: Dodgson — of the 'Dodgson, we've got Dodgson here!' scene — offers Nedry $1.5 million for fifteen embryos hidden in the shaving-cream can.

questions.question: In which Provençal town was the astrologer and seer Nostradamus born in 1503?
questions.note: Michel de Nostredame was born in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence in 1503 and later settled in nearby Salon-de-Provence, where he died.

questions.question: France set its statutory working week — the threshold beyond which hours count as overtime — at how many hours?
questions.note: The 'Aubry' laws fixed France's legal working week at 35 hours, in force from 2000.
